item.text:
# 1B.4 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is **mildly positive but thin** for 1B.4. Scholz clearly said he wanted a world where arms control mattered again, linked Germany’s security posture to Russia’s violation of past arms-control agreements, and supported multilateral de-escalatory framing. What I did **not** find is strong 2024 evidence of Scholz advancing a specific new arms-control, inspection, or disarmament agreement in a concrete negotiating sense.

## Accepted claim items

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **The Federal Chancellor’s 2024 summer press conference “I look forward to your questions”** | Federal Government | 24 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/chancellor-summer-press-conference-2024-2301040 | Scholz said long-range US weapons were being stationed in Germany to protect Germany and NATO states and to prevent war, and added that Russia had massively violated past arms-control agreements while “we all wish to live in a world where arms control plays an important role again.” This is the strongest direct 1B.4 evidence in 2024. | 1B.4, 1B.1 |
| **Speech by Olaf Scholz at "Summit of the Future Global Call"** | Federal Government | 12 Sep 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/speech-chancellor-summit-of-the-future-global-call-2308462 | Scholz explicitly said nuclear proliferation poses growing threats and framed the international order in terms of peace, stability, and multilateral repair. This supports a nonproliferation-minded posture, though it is not itself an agreement or inspection initiative. | 1B.4, 1B.2 |
| **Speech by Olaf Scholz, Chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany at the reception on the occasion of the Summit of the Future** | Federal Government | 23 Sep 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/speech-by-olaf-scholz-chancellor-of-the-federal-republic-of-germany-at-the-reception-on-the-occasion-of-the-summit-of-the-future-new-york-23-september-2024-2310980 | Scholz celebrated renewed commitment to the UN Charter, international law, and institutional reform of the international system. This is indirect but relevant evidence for good-faith support of de-escalatory multilateral arrangements. | 1B.4 |
| **Federal Chancellor Scholz’ press conference at the NATO Summit** | Federal Government | 12 Jul 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/service/archive/pc-chancellor-nato-summit-2298906 | Scholz emphasized NATO deterrence and alliance security rather than arms-control diplomacy. This is the main borderline counterweight: it does not show bad faith, but it shows that 2024 policy rhetoric leaned more toward deterrence than toward active arms-control bargaining. | 1B.4, 1B.1 |

## Counterevidence / limitations

- I found **no strong 2024 evidence** that Scholz personally pushed a specific new inspection regime, disarmament treaty, or verification mechanism.
- The strongest negative/borderline evidence is not anti-arms-control rhetoric; it is that his 2024 security messaging often prioritized **deterrence** after Russia’s violations of prior arms-control agreements.
- So the record is better read as **supportive in principle, limited in concrete arms-control output**.

## Synthesis for 1B.4

- **Most supported reading:** Scholz supported arms control, nonproliferation, and de-escalatory international order language in good faith.
- **Confidence level:** moderate, because the direct evidence is mostly rhetorical and multilateral rather than agreement-specific.
- **Main caveat:** 2024 practice centered on deterrence and support for Ukraine, not on launching a new arms-control bargain.
